facts.text: Kotzebue was originally called Kikiktagruk, meaning "almost an island," and served as a trading hub where rivers converged.
The city’s name honors Otto von Kotzebue, a Baltic German explorer who charted the sound while hunting the Northwest Passage in 1818.
Kotzebue hosts the Maniilaq Association, a tribally‑operated health and social services organization part of the Alaska Native Tribal Health Consortium.
In 1897, a reindeer station was established, later becoming the city’s first permanent settlement and a key point for Russian fur traders.
The Noatak, Selawik, and Kobuk Rivers empty into Kotzebue Sound, making the town a historic transportation center for inland communities.
Kotzebue Air Force Station, completed in 1958, operated a radar site until 1983, reflecting Cold War military presence in the Arctic.
